paper_title: $A'$ view of the sunrise: Boosting helioscopes with angular information
notes: New 90% CL exclusion limits on dark photon kinetic mixing epsilon from Hinode XRT solar X-ray telescope data, using two analyses: (1) 'darks' (calibration images, ~1 m baseline) covering roughly 3e-2 eV to keV masses, and (2) a 2012 solar eclipse image (~3.8e8 m baseline) extending sensitivity below ~1 meV down to ~2e-6 eV. Full limit curves are in figures 5 and 8 (not tabulated). Explicit numbers in text: Table 1 gives darks sensitivity epsilon~1e-9 at m=1 eV and eclipse epsilon~4e-8 at m=1 eV; figure 6 benchmarks (400 eV, 6.1e-11) and (15 eV, 1.2e-10) are stated to lie close to the exclusion limit (radial+spectral analysis without background subtraction), so they are approximate. The final data-driven background-subtracted darks limit is stronger by over an order of magnitude than the naive counting analysis. Not a DM search (solar production), so no local DM density assumed. First point (1 eV, 1e-9) is the darks limit; last point (1 eV, 4e-8) is the eclipse limit valid down to ~2e-6 eV. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 0, 0.6, 4))
